page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-24xCPU-256GB is a memory-optimized cloud server instance configured for high-capacity in-memory data processing. It is provisioned on the KVM hypervisor and powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 x86_64 processor operating at a base clock frequency of 2.0 GHz. The virtual machine allocates 24 shared vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores with 1 thread per core, backed by 64 KB L1d cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache. It incorporates 256 GB of system RAM, providing an abundant memory allocation ratio of 10.67 GB per vCPU.

The hardware configuration omits dedicated local storage and includes zero bundled GPUs, requiring external network-attached block volumes for persistent data storage. In compute and system evaluations, the instance demonstrates solid multi-core parallel throughput, achieving strong top-quartile performance in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (214.13 GB/sec) and a Geekbench multi-core score of 16550.0. In contrast, single-core execution reflects the modest 2.0 GHz clock speed, registering lower-tier results in single-threaded stress-ng tests.

Memory bandwidth benchmarks demonstrate uncached large-block read transfers of 123.14 GB/sec and write speeds of 72.86 GB/sec, while PassMark memory scoring falls into the bottom quartile. Redis SET operations reach 32.77 million operations per second, and static web serving delivers 17.15 GB/sec. Large language model inference tasks show average prompt processing but weak token generation metrics due to CPU-based execution without dedicated vector extensions such as AVX-512 or AMX.

Given its high memory-to-CPU ratio and shared CPU allocation model, UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-24xCPU-256GB delivers cost-efficient RAM density for memory-bound workloads. It is functionally suited for distributed caching layers, large in-memory databases, extract-transform-load (ETL) staging pipelines, and background data manipulation tasks that prioritize RAM capacity over extreme single-threaded compute speed.
